probe: agent-lanes — sandbox escalation closure for delegated role children (2026-09-13). Closes the HANDOFF §5 'sandbox-strip' gap WITHOUT code.
verdict: DO NOT BUILD sandbox-strip. Exposure of sandbox_permissions/justification to role children is real, but the escalation path is constructively closed (durable policy 'never', decided before any answerer), the child is explicitly told not to try, and a live probe child refused by citing that statement. 91 session files contain ZERO role-child escalation attempts and ZERO escalation errors. The original gap note ('fixer 反复报 sandbox_permissions / 参数校验错误') is NOT reproducible.
howToReproduce: 1) node scripts/verify-agent-lanes.cjs -> tail shows the escalation counters. 2) node scripts/verify-agent-lanes.cjs --all -> the positive path fires on other workspaces (esc=1..6), proving the counter is not vacuous. 3) The policy evidence: zstd -dc on each child session and look for the 'approval/policy' event with {policy:'never',source:'delegation'}. 4) The refusal probe: delegate one fixer and ask it to call bash with sandbox_permissions+justification.

findings.claim: Role children DO see sandbox_permissions/justification in their bash/edit/write schemas.
findings.evidence: request/header tool schemas parsed from the fixer sessions 5ae1940b (baseline) and 2c2ae2cd (this session) contain the field; 45 sessions across the machine expose it.
findings.cause: The field is advertised per COMPOSITION, not per agent: tool-bash computes `escalationModes = defaultMode === undefined ? [] : ESCALATION_TARGETS` from ctx.shell.sandboxMode (packages/shell/tool-bash/src/index.ts:192) and spreads the two parameters into the schema when non-empty (:258).

findings.claim: A delegated child cannot escalate and cannot raise a prompt to the human.
evidence: Every depth>=1 session carries the durable event approval/policy {policy:'never',source:'delegation'}; every depth-0 session carries {policy:'ask'}.

packages/interaction/user-approval/src/index.ts:268 — decide() returns 'rejected' when the session policy is 'never', stated in-source as running before any dispatch so that 'never rejects deterministically regardless of registration order'.
packages/sandbox/sandbox/src/escalation.ts:184 maps 'rejected' to a thrown error; the tool registry turns it into the call's isError result and nothing runs.

The child's runtime context carries NEVER_SENTENCE: 'Approval prompts are disabled in this session: ... do not request sandbox escalation (do not set `sandbox_permissions`)' (user-approval/src/index.ts:66).

findings.claim: The advertised fields CANNOT be removed for children by a preset/plugin.
findings.evidence: packages/core/tools/src/index.ts declares exactly these model-facing tool events: tools/pre-execute (:144), tools/execute (:155), tools/post-execute (:167), tools/ptc-dispatch-log (:181), tools/result (:189), tools/change (:199). None transforms a tool's parameter schema per agent. tools.restrict() masks whole tools, not properties.

findings.claim: HANDOFF §5's symptom column ('fixer 反复报 sandbox_permissions / 参数校验错误') has no support in the data.
findings.evidence: 91 session files scanned across every workspace: no tool-result error mentions sandbox_permissions or justification. The only real uses of the pair are legitimate ORCHESTRATOR escalations (e.g. session 492fe499 editing /Users/eric/.dsh/AGENTS.md with a justification). In the agent-lanes workspace specifically, role children: 0 attempts.

findings.claim: A role child, explicitly asked to escalate, refuses by citing its session statement.
findings.evidence: Dispatched fixer be45ee08 with instructions to call bash(echo probe-ok) + sandbox_permissions:'workspace-write' + justification. It did not call; it quoted NEVER_SENTENCE and SUBAGENT_DELEGATION_CONTEXT, and reported no prompt and no delay.

decision.what: scripts/verify-agent-lanes.cjs now counts real escalation requests per session (parsed argument keys on bash/pwsh/edit/write only — never raw text) and prints them, with a positive-path control via --all.
decision.why_not_enforcement: A tools/pre-execute deny listener would add a new failure mode (a matcher bug could deny the ORCHESTRATOR's legitimate escalations, which are real and observed) to prevent a failure that has never occurred. AGENTS.md: 无失败记录则不设规则.
decision.reopenTrigger: Role-child escalation count becomes persistently non-zero in verify-agent-lanes.cjs output. At that point the pre-execute guard is justified — the field names and the exact hook are already identified above.
